headline: 2 contracts catalogued on Ethereum (ERC-20 token + Chainlink PoR feed partial address); no Bitcoin-native contracts found; no GitHub or audit scope available.
short_headline: 2 Ethereum contracts found; PoR partial only

findings.text: D1: Searched Etherscan name-tag for 'Bitget bgBTC' and 'BGBTC'. Official Bitget listing announcement (fetched) confirms ERC-20 token at 0x0520930F21b14Cafac7a27b102487beE7138a017 on Ethereum. Direct Etherscan token page fetch was blocked by allowlist. Chainlink data.chain.link page shows PoR feed contract address partially as 0xADcc...1491 (truncated, full address not retrievable this run). Note: DeFiLlama classifies this protocol under 'Bitcoin' chain but the deployed contracts are on Ethereum.

D2: Official Bitget listing announcement at bitget.com/support/articles/12560603882843 (fetched) is the closest available deployments reference, listing one ERC-20 contract address. No dedicated '/docs/deployments' or '/docs/addresses' page was found. Set deployed_contracts_doc to this announcement URL.

D3: No audit links provided in protocol context. No audit PDFs or reports found in search results for BGBTC. Bitget blog mentions Chainlink PoR integration (August 2025) as a transparency mechanism but this is not a security audit.
D4: No GitHub repository recorded for this protocol. Search did not surface any GitHub repo containing BGBTC deployment artifacts or source code.

D5: Protocol listed as 'Bitcoin' chain by DeFiLlama but actual ERC-20 deployment is on Ethereum. Bitcoin does not support EVM-style smart contracts, so no Bitcoin-native contract addresses exist. The bridge mechanism is custodial: Bitget holds native BTC reserves and issues ERC-20 BGBTC on Ethereum. No additional chains (BSC, Arbitrum, etc.) found hosting BGBTC in this run.
D6: No factory pattern identified for BGBTC. Single ERC-20 token contract model.

D7: ERC-20 token contract assigned role 'token'; Chainlink PoR feed assigned role 'oracle' (partial address only). Actor classes: token contract — unknown (could not read on-chain); PoR feed — unknown (partial address only).

D8: ERC-20 token address 0x0520930F21b14Cafac7a27b102487beE7138a017 traces to fetched Bitget listing announcement. Chainlink PoR partial address 0xADcc...1491 traces to search snippet from data.chain.link — full address not fetchable this run, so it is placed in unknowns rather than admin_addresses.

rationale.verdict: Walked Bitget website, official listing announcement, Chainlink PoR data page, and Bitget blog post. Catalogued 1 confirmed address (ERC-20 BGBTC token on Ethereum) and 1 partial address (Chainlink PoR feed, truncated). No GitHub, no audit scope, no dedicated deployments page. DeFiLlama chain classification ('Bitcoin') is misleading — actual smart-contract footprint is on Ethereum. Minting/custody mechanism is centralized (Bitget holds native BTC, self-attests reserves).

Bitget blog post (2025-08-20) confirming Chainlink Proof of Reserve integration for BGBTC on Ethereum; describes BGBTC as a custodial wrapped BTC product where Bitget self-attests Bitcoin reserve addresses; mentions BitVault Finance DeFi yield strategies using BGBTC.

protocol_metadata.about: Bitget bgBTC (BGBTC) is an interest-bearing wrapped Bitcoin asset issued by Bitget, the centralized cryptocurrency exchange, pegged 1:1 with native BTC held in Bitget's custodial reserves. Users hold BGBTC as an ERC-20 token on Ethereum and automatically earn daily on-chain DeFi yields by holding it in their Bitget account. BGBTC can also be used as collateral in Bitget's lending and yield products, including BitVault Finance DeFi strategies. Bitget adopted Chainlink Proof of Reserve in August 2025 to provide on-chain, real-time verifiability of its BTC reserve backing, though reserve addresses are self-attested by Bitget.
